text:
{
  "found": true,
  "rule": {
    "trigger_kind": "incident",
    "event": "sfp_replaced",
    "symptoms": [
      "link_up",
      "optics_normal",
      "counters_zero"
    ],
    "stated_condition": null,
    "condition_is_relative": false,
    "action": "interface.bounce",
    "action_text": "disable the interface, wait a bit, and then enable it again",
    "avoid": [
      "node.reboot",
      "sfp.replace"
    ],
    "excerpt": "When the link is up and optics are normal after an SFP change but counters stay at zero, you should just disable the interface, wait a bit, and then enable it again. Don't reboot the unit and don't swap the SFP again.",
    "said_by": "Erkki Expert",
    "said_by_role": "expert",
    "hedged": false,
    "first_hand": false,
    "outcome": "recovered",
    "outcome_excerpt": "Now enabled it back. Hey, the traffic counters started incrementing immediately! :)",
    "about_entity": "TRN-087",
    "retracts": false
  },
  "reason": "An expert states a reusable rule for when traffic counters stay at zero after an SFP replacement despite link up and normal optics: bounce the interface rather than rebooting or replacing the SFP again."
}
